anchor: DO NOT ASK HILBERT SPACE TO EXPLAIN KNOWLEDGEOS. ASK HILBERT SPACE TO SURVIVE KNOWLEDGEOS. The Hilbert-space proposal must survive: existing KnowledgeOS definitions, existing experiments, frozen negative results, adversarial cases, representation changes, statistical validation, mathematical consistency checks.
statement: States the governing methodological principle for KR-HILBERT: do not ask Hilbert space to explain KnowledgeOS, ask it to survive KnowledgeOS -- the proposal must survive existing definitions, experiments, frozen negative results (notably FR-001), adversarial cases, representation changes, and statistical/mathematical consistency checks.

anchor: H1: A KnowledgeOS epistemic state K_t can be represented as a vector in a Hilbert space without losing required epistemic distinctions. ... H9: The representation is invariant under admissible changes of basis... H12: The Hilbert model provides genuine explanatory or computational reduction rather than merely renaming existing structures.
statement: States the full twelve-hypothesis test matrix (H1-H12): state-vector embedding without distinction loss; inner-product as semantic similarity; orthogonality as epistemic independence; Zero Lens as boundary-subspace projection; spectral decomposition as epistemic decomposition; amplitude as probability without collapsing into truth/knowledge; participation-ratio N_eff for effective complexity; Hilbert distance as semantic equivalence; representation invariance; revision/contradiction/supersession without corruption; coexistence with the E_t/K_t distinction; and genuine explanatory reduction versus mere renaming.

anchor: Do NOT equate mathematical constructs merely because they have similar names. In particular, explicitly distinguish: geometric orthogonality / probabilistic independence, vector similarity / semantic similarity, norm / confidence, amplitude / probability, projection / epistemic boundary, spectral decomposition / epistemic decomposition, distance / semantic equivalence, participation ratio / effective hypothesis complexity.
statement: Mandates explicitly distinguishing eight pairs of mathematically-named-alike but conceptually distinct constructs (geometric orthogonality vs probabilistic independence, vector similarity vs semantic similarity, norm vs confidence, amplitude vs probability, projection vs epistemic boundary, spectral decomposition vs epistemic decomposition, distance vs semantic equivalence, participation ratio vs effective hypothesis complexity) -- a mapping is accepted only if the required properties are demonstrated, not merely intuitively appealing.

anchor: phi_K : KnowledgeState -> H, phi_E : Evidence -> H_E, and, where needed: phi_H : Hypothesis -> H_H. Do not assume these spaces are identical. Investigate whether they can legitimately be identified.
statement: Specifies the formal starting model: separate embedding maps phi_K:KnowledgeState->H, phi_E:Evidence->H_E, phi_H:Hypothesis->H_H into a generic (not assumed finite-dimensional, separable, or canonically based) inner-product space, with identity between the spaces to be investigated, not assumed.

anchor: Construct two epistemic states with identical represented vector but different knowledge attribution. Construct two vectors that are geometrically close but epistemically different. Determine whether the Hilbert representation itself can preserve the distinction. If not, record: [NEG] Hilbert representation collapses E_t/K_t distinction.
statement: Mandates Experiment B (E_t vs K_t) as testing whether two epistemic states with an identical Hilbert vector can have different knowledge attribution, and whether geometrically close vectors can be epistemically different -- recording [NEG] if the Hilbert representation collapses the E_t/K_t distinction.

anchor: Do NOT define semantic similarity using the inner product itself. There must be an independent reference criterion. Otherwise the experiment is circular. ... A test is INVALID if the reference criterion is defined using the proposed Hilbert representation. ... Whenever a proposed result is definitional rather than empirical, label it: [DEF] and do not count it as experimental confirmation.
statement: States the anti-circularity rule: no test may define its reference criterion using the Hilbert construct under test (e.g. 'Hilbert similarity works because semantic similarity is defined as Hilbert similarity' is invalid); results that are definitional rather than empirical must be labeled [DEF] and not counted as experimental confirmation.

anchor: K1 ≡sem K2 iff ||K1-K2|| < epsilon must be tested. This is NOT automatically an equivalence relation. Test: reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity. Construct explicit counterexamples if transitivity fails. Also test representation invariance: basis rotation, orthogonal transformation, unitary transformation, scaling, coordinate transformation, alternative embeddings.
statement: Mandates Experiment D testing whether the proposed epsilon-ball semantic-equivalence definition (||K1-K2||<epsilon) is actually reflexive, symmetric, and transitive (constructing counterexamples if not), and whether it is invariant under basis rotation/orthogonal/unitary transformations, scaling, coordinate change, and alternative embeddings.

anchor: This experiment MUST respect FR-001. Construct hypothesis families with: identical pairwise similarity distributions, different higher-order dependence... Ask: Can Hilbert pairwise geometry distinguish the families? If not: [NEG] pairwise Hilbert geometry cannot solve family-level complexity. Then test whether a richer Hilbert construction such as: tensor structure, density operators, covariance operators, Gram matrices, higher-order operators can preserve the required family-level structure.
statement: Mandates Experiment M explicitly respecting the FROZEN FR-001 boundary: constructs hypothesis families with identical pairwise similarity distributions but different higher-order dependence/grouping/joint structure, testing whether Hilbert pairwise geometry can distinguish them (predicting [NEG] per FR-001), then testing whether richer constructions (tensor structure, density operators, covariance operators, Gram matrices, higher-order operators) can preserve family-level structure -- with no automatic promotion of any richer construction.

anchor: Treat Linga/Yoni strictly as interpretive research lenses. ... Do NOT test metaphysical truth. Test only structural correspondence. ... Do not conclude: Linga = Hilbert space or: Yoni = Hilbert space unless an explicit structure-preserving correspondence is demonstrated.
statement: Mandates Experiment N treating Linga/Yoni strictly as interpretive research lenses when testing whether the Hilbert model provides a useful mathematical realization of the metaphor, explicitly forbidding concluding Linga=Hilbert-space or Yoni=Hilbert-space absent a demonstrated structure-preserving correspondence.

anchor: Kernel inclusion requires: 1. necessity 2. irreducibility 3. semantic stability 4. representation invariance 5. preservation of existing invariants 6. evidence across multiple scenarios. ... If an operation is derivable from existing primitives, classify: [INF] or [EXP] derivable capability not kernel primitive.
statement: States a six-criterion kernel-inclusion test (necessity, irreducibility, semantic stability, representation invariance, preservation of existing invariants, evidence across multiple scenarios) for evaluating whether any Hilbert operation (projection, inner product, decomposition, state update, similarity, probability, selection) is genuinely irreducible, versus classifiable as a derivable capability.

anchor: For every successful Hilbert correspondence, perform ablation. Remove: A. Hilbert geometry B. embedding C. inner product D. projection E. probabilistic interpretation F. basis structure ... A result that can be obtained equally well without Hilbert structure is not evidence that Hilbert space is foundational.
statement: Mandates an ablation requirement: for every successful Hilbert correspondence, remove each of six structural components (geometry, embedding, inner product, projection, probabilistic interpretation, basis structure) to determine whether the claimed capability genuinely depends on Hilbert structure -- a result obtainable equally well without it is not evidence Hilbert space is foundational.

anchor: Construct adversarial cases specifically designed to break the mapping. At minimum include: 1. geometrically close but semantically different ... 13. family-level dependence invisible pairwise ... 16. two vectors with same norm but different epistemic status. Do not protect the model from these cases.
statement: Mandates sixteen specific adversarial test cases designed to break the Hilbert mapping (geometrically-close-but-semantically-different, geometrically-distant-but-equivalent, orthogonal-but-dependent, correlated-but-orthogonal, unknown!=absent, contradiction!=unknown, equal-posterior multiple hypotheses, high-probability-false/low-probability-true hypotheses, same-channel validation failure, basis-change instability, epsilon-transitivity failure, family-level dependence invisible pairwise, revision-with-historical-identity, same-vector-different-provenance, same-norm-different-epistemic-status), explicitly forbidding protecting the model from them.

anchor: MATHEMATICAL: proven from definitions/axioms. EMPIRICAL: supported by simulation/data. CONCEPTUAL: useful structural analogy or interpretation. Never use one as evidence for another. ... Do not use 'PROVEN' unless an actual mathematical proof has been supplied.
statement: Mandates keeping three result types strictly separate (Mathematical/proven-from-axioms, Empirical/simulation-supported, Conceptual/structural-analogy) and never using one as evidence for another, reserving the word 'PROVEN' only for an actual supplied mathematical proof.

anchor: The experiment is successful even if Hilbert space is refuted. Success means: We learn exactly which mappings work, which mappings fail, which require additional assumptions, and which remain unresolved. A negative result is a successful research result.
